name: Adam
footnote: First human formed from the ground; his name is literally what he was made from.

name: Eve
footnote: Mother of all living; the name given after the promise of redemption.

name: Cain
footnote: Eve said, “I have acquired a man with the help of the LORD,” but he became the first murderer.

name: Abel
footnote: His life was short and vanished like a breath; the first martyr.

name: Seth
footnote: God appointed another seed instead of Abel; the chosen line continues through him.

name: Enos
footnote: The familiar English form is Enos; the Hebrew form is usually represented as Enosh, meaning man, mortal, or frail.

name: Cainan
footnote: The familiar English form in this LXX/KJV genealogy is Cainan; the related Hebrew form is often represented as Kenan.

name: Mahalaleel
meaning: Praise of God; the shining one of God
footnote: Familiar English form for this genealogy; his name carries praise-of-God language.

name: Jared
footnote: Traditional interpretation points to descent or coming judgment.

name: Enoch
footnote: Cain's son and city namesake here; the same familiar English name is later used for the Sethite Enoch who pleased God.

name: Methuselah
meaning: When he dies, it shall be sent; man of the dart
footnote: His death coincided with the Flood; his name is often taken as a prophecy of judgment.

name: Lamech
meaning: Powerful; overthrower; possibly poor or despairing
footnote: Cainite descendant who takes two wives and speaks the violence song; the same familiar English name later appears for Noah's father.

name: Noah
footnote: The ark brought rest from judgment.

name: Shem
footnote: Ancestor of the Semitic line; through him came the line that would bear God’s name.

name: Japheth
footnote: His descendants spread across the earth.

name: Abram
footnote: His original name emphasizes fatherhood before the covenant expansion of his name.

name: Abraham
footnote: God expanded Abram's name to mark the covenant promise that many nations would come from him.

name: Sara
footnote: The LXX form appears before the covenant-renaming narrative.

name: Sarai
footnote: Her earlier name anticipates the covenant name Sarah.

name: Sarah
footnote: God renamed Sarai as Sarah in the covenant promise of Isaac.

name: Hagar
footnote: Egyptian servant of Sarah; God saw and heard her affliction in the wilderness.

name: Isaac
footnote: His name answers Abraham and Sarah's laughter and marks the promised son.

name: Lot
footnote: Abraham's nephew, rescued from captivity and later from Sodom.

name: Melchizedek
footnote: King of Salem and priest of God Most High; later read typologically in Hebrews.

name: Rebekah
footnote: Chosen as Isaac's wife and mother of Jacob and Esau.

name: Leah
footnote: Jacob's first wife; mother of Judah and Levi.

name: Rachel
footnote: Beloved wife of Jacob and mother of Joseph and Benjamin.

name: Canaan
footnote: Name of Ham's son and of the land later promised to Abraham's seed.

name: Ishmael
footnote: God heard Hagar’s affliction in the wilderness.

name: Pharaoh
footnote: Egyptian royal title used as a personal designation for Egypt's king.

name: Abimelech
footnote: Royal name or title borne by rulers in the patriarchal and judges narratives.

name: Laban
footnote: Rebekah's brother and Jacob's Aramean father-in-law.

name: Esau
footnote: Born hairy and red; sold his birthright for red stew.

name: Jacob
footnote: Grabbed Esau’s heel at birth; later supplanted him and became Israel.

name: Israel
footnote: Wrestled with God and prevailed; name of the covenant nation.

name: Reuben
footnote: Leah’s first son; hoped it would win Jacob’s love.

name: Simeon
footnote: The LORD heard that Leah was hated.

name: Levi
footnote: Leah hoped her husband would be joined to her; tribe of priests.

name: Judah
footnote: Royal tribe and ancestor of Messiah.

name: Dan
footnote: Rachel named him from God's judgment in her favor through Bilhah's son.

name: Gad
footnote: Leah's household named him with fortune/troop language.

name: Asher
footnote: Leah called him happy because women would call her blessed.

name: Issachar
footnote: Leah named him from the reward or wages theme in the birth story.

name: Zebulun
footnote: Leah linked the name with her hope that Jacob would dwell with her.

name: Joseph
footnote: God added to his blessings despite betrayal; savior of his family.

name: Ephraim
footnote: Joseph named him because God made him fruitful in the land of affliction.

name: Manasseh
footnote: Joseph named him because God made him forget his toil and father's house.

name: Benjamin
footnote: Rachel’s son of sorrow became son of the right hand.

name: Moses
footnote: Drawn out of the Nile; drew Israel out of Egypt.

name: Aaron
footnote: First high priest; exalted to lead worship.

name: Nadab
footnote: Aaron's son whose priestly privilege ended in judgment for unauthorized fire.

name: Ithamar
footnote: Aaron's son; priestly line continued through him.

name: Joshua
footnote: Led Israel into the Promised Land; his name points to the ultimate Savior.

name: Balaam
footnote: Foreign diviner whose blessing-oracles God turned toward Israel's good.

name: Caleb
footnote: Followed the LORD fully; faithful like a dog.

name: Gideon
footnote: Judge who cut down Baal's altar and was raised to deliver Israel.

name: Jephthae
footnote: Gileadite judge whose name fits his opening of negotiations and battle.

name: Samson
footnote: Judge whose strength burned brightly but whose story ended in costly judgment.

name: Elimelech
footnote: Naomi's husband; his name confesses God as king in the days of the judges.

name: Naomi
footnote: Ruth's mother-in-law; her bitter season was reversed by covenant kindness.

name: Mahlon
footnote: Naomi's son; his death leaves Ruth widowed before redemption enters the story.

name: Chilion
footnote: Naomi's son; his name is traditionally linked with frailty or wasting.

name: Orpah
footnote: Ruth's sister-in-law who turned back to Moab.

name: Boaz
footnote: Kinsman-redeemer in Ruth; ancestor of David.

name: Rahab
footnote: God’s mercy was broad enough to save a Canaanite prostitute.

name: Ruth
footnote: Loyal friend to Naomi; became ancestor of David and Messiah.

name: Heli
footnote: Priest at Shiloh who judged Israel and raised Samuel.

name: Elkana
meaning: God has acquired; God has created
footnote: Hannah's husband and father of Samuel.

name: Samuel
meaning: Heard of God; God has heard
footnote: God heard Hannah’s prayer; last judge and anointer of kings.

name: Saul
footnote: The people asked for a king; first king of Israel.

name: Jonathan
footnote: Saul's son and David's covenant friend.

name: Abner
footnote: Commander in Saul's house whose name carries light/father imagery.

name: David
footnote: The beloved king; a man after God’s own heart.

name: Nabal
footnote: His name matches the folly Abigail explicitly exposes.

name: Joab
footnote: David's powerful commander, loyal and dangerous in equal measure.

name: Absalom
footnote: David's son whose peaceful name contrasts with rebellion and grief.

name: Nathan
footnote: Prophet who confronted David and guarded the promise line.

name: Ourias
footnote: The Hittite whose faithful conduct exposed David's sin.

name: Mephibosthe
meaning: From the mouth of shame; dispeller of shame
footnote: Jonathan's son whom David restored to table fellowship.

name: Solomon
footnote: Brought peace and built the Temple.

name: Sadok
footnote: Priest whose line became central to temple priesthood.

name: Abiathar
footnote: Priest who survived Nob and served David before being removed by Solomon.

name: Rehoboam
footnote: Solomon's son whose reign split the kingdom.

name: Jeroboam
meaning: The people increase; he contends for the people
footnote: First king of the northern kingdom after the split.

name: Ahab
footnote: Northern king whose reign is remembered for Baal worship and Elijah's confrontation.

name: Elijah
footnote: Confronted Baal worship with the truth that Yahweh alone is God.

name: Elisha
footnote: Continued Elijah’s work; brought salvation and healing.

name: Asa
footnote: Judahite king remembered for reforms and imperfect late reliance.

name: Hezekiah
footnote: Judahite king strengthened by the LORD during Assyrian threat.

name: Josiah
footnote: Reforming king whose name fits the restoration of covenant worship.

name: Jehoiakim
footnote: Judahite king raised by Egypt but judged for resisting Jeremiah's word.

name: Zedekiah
footnote: Last king of Judah before Jerusalem fell to Babylon.

name: Nebuchadnezzar
meaning: Nabu, protect my boundary or heir
footnote: Babylonian king used as an instrument of judgment against Judah.

name: Cyrus
footnote: Persian king named in restoration promises and used to return Judah from exile.

name: Darius
meaning: Holder of the good; one who holds firm
footnote: Persian royal name borne by kings connected with temple-era events.

name: Artaxerxes
footnote: Persian royal name prominent in Esther and Ezra-Nehemiah settings.

name: Mardochaios
meaning: Little man; possibly devoted to Marduk
footnote: Greek form used for Mordecai, Esther's cousin and guardian.

name: Aman
footnote: Enemy of the Jews whose apparent greatness collapsed under providential reversal.

name: Isaiah
footnote: Prophesied the coming Savior.

name: Jeremiah
footnote: Exalted God even while weeping over Jerusalem.

name: Baruch
footnote: Jeremiah's scribe whose name means blessed.

name: Ezekiel
footnote: Strengthened by God during exile.

name: Daniel
footnote: Stood before earthly kings while God remained his true Judge.

name: Job
footnote: Righteous sufferer whose name is traditionally explained in more than one way.

name: Hosea
footnote: His life pictured God’s faithful salvation of unfaithful Israel.

name: Jonah
footnote: Fled yet brought salvation to Nineveh.

name: Micah
footnote: A rhetorical question pointing to God’s uniqueness.

name: Nahum
footnote: Brought comfort by announcing the end of Nineveh’s oppression.

name: Habakkuk
footnote: Embraced God in faith despite coming judgment.

name: Zephaniah
footnote: Hidden and protected the remnant during judgment.

name: Haggai
footnote: Urged the people to rebuild the Temple.

name: Zechariah
footnote: God remembered His covenant promises.

name: Malachi
footnote: The last Old Testament messenger before John the Baptist.

name: Esther
footnote: Hidden like a star; saved her people.

name: Mordecai
footnote: Humble servant who refused to bow to Haman.

name: Ezra
footnote: Helped restore the Law and the people after exile.

name: Nehemiah
footnote: Comforted and rebuilt Jerusalem’s walls.

name: Mary
footnote: Mother of Jesus; experienced bitterness yet exaltation.

name: Joseph (NT)
footnote: God added protection and provision for the holy family.

name: John
footnote: Forerunner of Jesus; proclaimed God’s grace.

name: Jesus
footnote: He will save His people from their sins.

name: Peter
footnote: The rock-like apostle.

name: Andrew
footnote: Courageous fisherman turned fisher of men.

name: James
footnote: One of the sons of thunder; later a pillar of the Church.

name: Philip
footnote: Brought people to Jesus.

name: Bartholomew
footnote: Jesus called him an Israelite in whom is no deceit.

name: Thomas
footnote: Later confessed, “My Lord and my God!”

name: Matthew
footnote: Tax collector given the gift of apostleship and authorship.

name: Simon the Zealot
footnote: Zealous revolutionary transformed into apostle.

name: Judas (not Iscariot)
footnote: Praised God; associated with the epistle of Jude.

name: Paul
footnote: Changed from Saul to Paul, the humble apostle to the Gentiles.

name: Timothy
footnote: Paul’s faithful son in the faith.

name: Titus
footnote: Defended the faith and organized churches.

name: Philemon
footnote: Showed affectionate forgiveness to Onesimus.

name: Barnabas
footnote: Encouraged the early Church and Paul.

name: Stephen
footnote: Received the martyr’s crown.

name: Lydia
footnote: Dealer in purple; first European convert.

name: Aquila
footnote: Strong teacher alongside Priscilla.

name: Priscilla
footnote: Venerable teacher alongside her husband.

name: Apollos
footnote: Mighty preacher whose eloquence was refined.

name: Silas
footnote: Steady companion who endured prison with Paul.

name: Onesimus
footnote: The runaway slave who became useful.

name: Phoebe
footnote: Radiant servant who carried Paul’s letter to Rome.

name: Gaius
footnote: Hospitable host who brought joy to the Church.

name: Erastus
footnote: Beloved city treasurer who served Paul.

name: Demas
footnote: Loved this present world and forsook Paul.

name: Mark
footnote: Initially faltered but later became useful to Paul.

name: Luke
footnote: Beloved physician who brought gospel light.

name: Theophilus
footnote: The one Luke wrote to.

name: Diotrephes
footnote: Loved preeminence and opposed apostolic authority.

name: Gamaliel
footnote: Wise teacher who advised the Sanhedrin.

name: Nicodemus
footnote: Came to Jesus by night seeking truth.

name: Lazarus
footnote: Raised from the dead.

name: Martha
footnote: Busy homemaker who learned to sit at Jesus’ feet.

name: Mary Magdalene
footnote: First witness to the resurrection.

name: Salome
footnote: Associated with the disciples and the resurrection narratives.

name: Barabbas
footnote: Released in place of the true Son of the Father.

name: Pilate
footnote: Roman judge who washed his hands of Jesus.

name: Herod
footnote: Name borne by multiple rulers who opposed God’s plan.

name: Ananias
footnote: Name borne by multiple figures in the New Testament.

name: Sapphira
footnote: Beautiful exterior but deceptive heart.

name: Cornelius
footnote: Roman centurion turned to God.

name: Felix
footnote: Trembled before the truth yet never found true happiness.

name: Festus
footnote: Roman governor who heard Paul’s defense.

name: Agrippa
footnote: Heard the gospel but remained untamed.

name: Bernice
footnote: Present at Paul’s trial.

name: Artemas
footnote: Faithful coworker Paul sent to Crete.

name: Tychicus
footnote: Trusted messenger who carried Paul’s letters.

name: Epaphras
footnote: Fervent intercessor for Colossae.

name: Archippus
footnote: Called to fulfill his ministry.

name: Apphia
footnote: Hostess connected with a growing house church.

name: Euodia
footnote: Worked hard in the gospel but needed unity.

name: Syntyche
footnote: Called to agree in the Lord.

name: Clement
footnote: Fellow worker whose name is in the Book of Life.

name: Epaphroditus
footnote: Risked his life to serve Paul.

name: Onesiphorus
footnote: Refreshing and profitable servant.

name: Aristarchus
footnote: Loyal companion and fellow prisoner.

name: Zacchaeus
footnote: Tax collector made pure by Jesus.

name: Bartimaeus
footnote: Blind beggar healed and then followed Jesus.

name: Jairus
footnote: His daughter was raised.

name: Simeon (NT)
footnote: Held baby Jesus and declared he had seen salvation.

name: Anna
footnote: Prophetess who recognized the Messiah.

name: Elizabeth
footnote: Mother of John; God kept His oath.

name: Zacharias
footnote: Father of John; God remembered him.

name: John the Baptist
footnote: Prepared the way with grace.

name: Herodias
footnote: Manipulative figure who sought John’s head.

name: Cleopas
footnote: Disciple on the Emmaus road.

name: Matthias
footnote: Chosen to replace Judas.

name: Philip (evangelist)
footnote: Evangelized Samaria and the Ethiopian eunuch.

name: Simon the Sorcerer
footnote: Heard the gospel but sought power.

name: Dorcas
footnote: Full of good works and raised to life.

name: Sergius Paulus
footnote: Proconsul who believed after seeing God’s power.

name: Elymas
footnote: Sorcerer who opposed the gospel.

name: Jason
footnote: Hosted Paul and faced riot.

name: Dionysius
footnote: Areopagite who believed Paul’s message.

name: Damaris
footnote: Athenian woman who joined the believers.

name: Gallio
footnote: Dismissed charges against Paul.

name: Alexander
footnote: The coppersmith who strongly opposed Paul.

name: Hymenaeus
footnote: False teacher who shipwrecked faith.

name: Phygelus
footnote: Deserted Paul in Asia.

name: Hermogenes
footnote: Also deserted Paul.

name: Crescens
footnote: Faithful coworker who went to Galatia.

name: Pudens
footnote: Roman Christian who greeted Paul.

name: Linus
footnote: Early Christian leader.

name: Claudia
footnote: Woman who greeted Paul.

name: Eubulus
footnote: Faithful in Rome.

name: Zenas
footnote: Lawyer who traveled with Apollos.

name: Jude
footnote: Author of the epistle of Jude.

name: Sosthenes
footnote: Associated with Corinth and with Paul.

name: Crispus
footnote: Synagogue ruler baptized by Paul.

name: Fortunatus
footnote: Corinthian who refreshed Paul.

name: Achaicus
footnote: Helped Paul.

name: Stephanas
footnote: Among the first converts in Achaia.

name: Chloe
footnote: Associated with the report of divisions in Corinth.

name: Nymphas
footnote: Hosted a house church.
